1. (11) (Currently amended): A method for training a molecular properties model, comprising: obtaining a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules, wherein the pseudo partial ordering includes at least a representation of a first and second molecule, ordered relative to one another and a property of interest; __generating a representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm__; and __executing the selected machine learning algorithm on a computer processor using the pseudo partial ordering to train a molecular properties model configured to generate a prediction regarding additional molecules supplied to the model__.

2. (12) (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the molecular properties model generates predictions related to a property of interest selected from at least one of a pharmacokinetic property, pharmacodynamic property, physiological or pharmacological activity, toxicity or selectivity; a chemical property including reactivity, binding affinity, pKa, or a property of a specific atom or bond in a molecule; or a physical property including melting point, solubility, a membrane permeability, and a force-field parameter; __wherein the property of interest is determined by measuring molecules that are ordered relative to one another based on quantitative differences in the property of interest__.

3. (13) (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a classification learning algorithm __that is executed on a computer processor to classify molecules based on the pseudo-partial ordering__.

4. (14) (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a kernel based learning algorithm __that is executed on a computer processor to process the pseudo-partial ordering of molecules__.

5. (15) (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a variant of a Boosting algorithm, RankBoost algorithm, Alternating Decision Trees algorithm, Support Vector Machines algorithm, a Perceptron algorithm, Winnow, a Hedge Algorithm, decision trees, neural networks, genetic algorithms, genetic programming or any modifications thereof __modified to process the pseudo partial ordering of ranked pairs and executed on a computer processor__.

6. (16) (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is executed on a computer processor and is configured to minimize, either directly or indirectly, an area above, or below, a receiver operator characteristic curve __based on the pseudo-partial ordering of molecules__.

7. (17) (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is executed on a computer processor and is configured to minimize, either directly or indirectly, a function of the rank ordering of molecules in the pseudo partial ordering.

8. (19) (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein generating the representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules comprises: generating a vector representation of the molecules on a computer processor, wherein the vector representation is configured to encode the structure of the molecules included the pseudo-partial ordering; or comprises generating an n-point pharmacophore representation of the molecules included in the pseudo-partial ordering __on a computer processor__.

9. (20) (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein a threshold value or cutoff molecule is selected for the molecular proprieties model on a computer processor and used to create a classification model.

10. (21) (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the at least one additional molecule comprises two or more additional molecules, and wherein the prediction comprises a ranked ordering of the two or more additional molecules, relative to one another and to the property of interest, __wherein the ranked ordering is generated by the molecular properties model executed on a computer processor__.

11. (22) (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein at least two of the molecules in the pseudo-partial ordering are alternative representations of the same physical molecule and the property of interest is a property of the alternative representations, __wherein the alternative representations are generated and compared on a computer processor__.

12. (23) (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein at least two of the molecules in the pseudo-partial ordering are encoded on a computer processor to represent different atoms, bonds or substituent groups of the same molecule and the property of interest is a property of the atoms, bonds or substituent groups.

13. (35) (Currently amended): A computer-storage medium __that is non-transitory__ containing a program which, when executed by a processor, performs a method for training a molecular properties model, comprising: receiving a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules, wherein the pseudo partial ordering includes at least a representation of a first and second molecule, ordered relative to one another and a property of interest; generating a representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm on the processor; providing the pseudo partial ordering of molecules to the selected machine learning algorithm; executing the selected machine learning algorithm on the processor using the pseudo partial ordering to train a molecular properties model configured to generate a prediction regarding additional molecules supplied to the model.
